recaps.title: Opening

recaps.text: No characters, places or events of the story appear, so the reader learns only that the book is built from diaries, journals, letters and a newspaper cutting.
recaps.title: Contents

recaps.text: Harker travels east through Hungary and Transylvania, keeping a shorthand journal and researching the region in London beforehand. In Bistritz the innkeepers seem frightened by his mention of Count Dracula, and the landlady begs him not to travel on St. George's Eve. Harker sets out by coach through the Carpathians, where the passengers make warding signs against the evil eye and pity him. At the Borgo Pass no carriage from the Count is waiting, and a strange, powerful driver takes Harker onward in a calèche. On the midnight journey wolves surround the carriage and blue flames flicker by the road, frightening Harker. The carriage reaches a vast ruined castle in the moonlight, where Harker's journey ends in unsettling uncertainty.
recaps.title: CHAPTER I JONATHAN HARKER’S JOURNAL

recaps.text: Jonathan Harker, a young English solicitor, travelled to Transylvania at the request of Count Dracula to help with the purchase of a London estate at Purfleet, called Carfax. Warned by frightened villagers and strange omens along the way, he reached the Count's vast ruined castle at night, where Dracula welcomed him. Dracula has been polite and hospitable, though Harker has noticed unnatural signs about him: no reflections, no servants, no eating, and a violent reaction to blood and the crucifix. Harker has also noticed the atlas rings near London, Exeter and Whitby. Harker now knows that the castle is locked and that he cannot leave, and he is uneasy about what Dracula really intends.

Harker arrives at the castle late at night and is welcomed in by Count Dracula, who carries his luggage and feeds him supper. Dracula explains that his gout keeps him from travelling and that a young servant will assist Harker with the London estate. Over the next days Harker and Dracula discuss England, and Dracula asks Harker to help him perfect his English. Dracula talks about the blue flames as signs of hidden treasure and reviews the Purfleet estate papers, which he signs. Harker notices rings marked on an atlas near London, Exeter and Whitby, and finds nothing else in the castle that he can read. Dracula is startled at the sight of Harker's blood after he cuts himself shaving, and reacts with fury until he sees the crucifix. Dracula destroys the shaving glass, leaving Harker unable to shave properly. Harker finds every door locked and concludes that the castle is a prison and that he is a prisoner.
recaps.title: CHAPTER II JONATHAN HARKER’S JOURNAL—continued

recaps.text: Jonathan Harker, a young English solicitor, travelled to Transylvania to help Count Dracula buy the London estate of Carfax at Purfleet. Warned by frightened villagers and omens, he reached the Count's ruined castle at night and was welcomed, but he has since noticed unnatural signs about Dracula and found that every door is locked. Harker now knows he is a prisoner. Dracula has been questioning him about English business and shipping, has insisted he stay another month, and has handed him letters that he will read. Harker secretly read the Count's letters to bankers and agents in London, Varna and Buda-Pesth. Dracula has warned him never to sleep outside his own rooms, and Harker has placed a crucifix above his bed. After seeing Dracula climb down the castle wall, Harker fell asleep in the old women's rooms and was visited by three pale women. Dracula stopped them, declaring Harker belongs to him, and the women vanished with a moving bag. Harker, terrified and locked in, now faces an uncertain future with the Count.

Harker realises he is a prisoner and decides to hide his fears and knowledge from Dracula. Dracula questions Harker about English legal business, shipping and consignments, and Harker realises the Count is preparing for dealings in England. Dracula insists that Harker stay another month and hands him letters home, which he will read. Harker secretly reads the Count's letters, addressed to bankers and agents in London, Varna and Buda-Pesth. Dracula warns Harker never to sleep anywhere in the castle except his own rooms, and Harker places a crucifix above his bed. Harker sees Dracula climb head-first down the castle wall and vanish, and later discovers a locked hall door with its key gone. Harker falls asleep in the old women's rooms despite the warning and is visited by three pale women who gather around him. Dracula bursts in, drives the women away and declares that Harker belongs to him alone, then the women vanish with a moving bag, and Harker faints.
recaps.title: CHAPTER III JONATHAN HARKER’S JOURNAL—continued

recaps.text: Jonathan Harker, a young English solicitor, travelled to Transylvania to help Count Dracula buy the London estate of Carfax at Purfleet, and was welcomed at the Count's castle. He has since learned that the Count is a monster, that his doors are locked, and that the Count and three pale women mean to keep him. The Count has forced Harker to write letters home post-dated to later dates, and has taken his papers and clothes. Harker has seen the Count wear his clothes to deceive others and has witnessed a murdered woman and the Count lying gorged with blood in an earth-filled box. The Count has announced that Harker will leave, but Harker finds the great door bolted again and is trapped in the Count's room as the Szgany and Slovaks load the boxes and depart. Harker now plans to climb down the castle wall, take some gold, and escape to England, though he is unsure whether he will succeed.

Harker wakes unsure whether the Count carried him to bed, and finds the room at the top of the stairs forced shut, convincing him his fright was real. The Count makes Harker write post-dated letters falsely saying he is leaving, dated to be sent later, and Harker realises from the dates that his life has little time left. Harker gets a letter to Peter Hawkins out through a Szgany band camped in the courtyard, but the Count later opens it, burns an unsigned letter, and forces Harker to reseal the first. Harker discovers his papers, notes, letter of credit and travelling clothes are gone, leaving him without means to escape the castle. Harker watches the Count leave the castle wearing Harker's own clothes, a sign that the Count means to let others believe Harker is still travelling and posting letters. A woman appears in the courtyard demanding her child from the Count, and wolves called by him tear her apart, showing Harker what has happened to the child. Harker climbs the castle wall into the Count's empty room, finds a hoard of old gold and a chapel with earth-filled boxes, and discovers the Count lying in one of them, apparently dead yet warm. The Count announces that Harker will leave the next day, but when he opens the great door wolves rush in, and Harker begs him to shut it and wait until morning. Harker learns the main door is bolted again, and returns to the Count's room to find the Count gorged with blood; he strikes at him with a shovel, but the Count's gaze stops the blow. As the Szgany and Slovaks arrive to load the boxes and leave, Harker is trapped in the Count's room by a sudden gust that shuts the stair door. Harker resolves to climb down the wall, carrying some gold, to escape the castle and reach England.
recaps.title: CHAPTER IV JONATHAN HARKER’S JOURNAL—continued

recaps.text: Jonathan Harker, a young English solicitor, travelled to Transylvania to help Count Dracula buy the London estate of Carfax, and was welcomed at the Count's castle. He has since discovered that the Count is a monster who keeps him prisoner, takes his papers and clothes, and has forced him to write post-dated letters. Harker has seen a murdered woman and the Count lying gorged with blood in an earth-filled box. The Count has left the castle wearing Harker's clothes, and Harker, trapped in the Count's room as the Szgany and Slovaks load the boxes to depart, plans to climb down the wall with some gold and escape to England. In England, Mina Murray, engaged to Jonathan, writes to her friend Lucy Westenra about her hopes and her shorthand practice. Lucy admits her love for an unnamed man and reports that Dr. Seward and Quincey Morris have both proposed and been refused. Seward is troubled and turns to his patient Renfield, and Morris invites Arthur and Seward to a gathering. Harker's escape and the fate of the Count remain unresolved.

Mina writes to Lucy about her shorthand practice and her engagement to Jonathan, and asks for news of a curly-haired man. Lucy confesses her love for an unnamed man and reports that she received three proposals in one day. Dr. Seward and Quincey Morris each propose to Lucy, and she turns them down, Morris accepting her choice with grace. Seward, troubled by his rejection, turns to his patient Renfield and resolves to understand his strange mind. Morris invites Arthur and Seward to a gathering, and Arthur replies that he will attend and has messages to deliver.
recaps.title: CHAPTER V

recaps.text: Jonathan Harker, a young English solicitor, travelled to Transylvania to help Count Dracula buy London property and was held prisoner in the Count's castle. He discovered that the Count is a monster, saw a murdered woman and the Count gorged with blood in an earth-filled box, then escaped the castle by climbing down the wall. In England, Mina Murray is engaged to Jonathan and writes to Lucy Westenra, who confesses her love for an unnamed man and has refused proposals from Dr. Seward and Quincey Morris. Seward has begun studying his patient Renfield, a fly-eating patient who has now devoured his sparrows. At Whitby, Mina visits Lucy and talks with the sceptical old sailor Mr. Swales, while Lucy waits for her fiancé Arthur, delayed by his father's illness. Mina has received a short letter from Jonathan dated from Castle Dracula, and her anxiety grows as Lucy walks in her sleep. Jonathan's fate and whether the Count has reached England remain unresolved, and a strange Russian ship is sighted off the coast as a storm approaches.

Mina arrives at Whitby, where she meets Lucy and sees the town, abbey and churchyard, and spends time with Mr. Swales. Mr. Swales mocks local legends and the lies carved on tombstones, and reveals that one gravestone hides a suicide. Lucy tells Mina about her marriage to Arthur, while Mina feels anxious that Jonathan has not written for a month. Dr. Seward studies Renfield, whose fly-eating and notebook of figures lead Seward to conclude he is a zoophagous maniac. Renfield's tame sparrows vanish, and after he eats one raw Seward drugs him and considers using him in an experiment. Mina receives a short, unsettling letter from Jonathan dated from Castle Dracula, saying he is starting for home. Lucy's walking in her sleep worsens, and Mina locks their door each night at Mrs. Westenra's request. Arthur is delayed by his father's serious illness, so his visit to Lucy is postponed. Mina, still without news, grows more anxious and feels that Lucy watches her even in sleep. A storm approaches Whitby, and a strange Russian ship is sighted by the coastguard.
recaps.title: CHAPTER VI MINA MURRAY’S JOURNAL

recaps.text: Jonathan Harker, a young English solicitor, travelled to Transylvania to help Count Dracula buy London property, was held prisoner in his castle, discovered the Count is a monster, and escaped by climbing down the wall. In England, Mina Murray is engaged to Jonathan and worries about his silence, while her friend Lucy Westenra has refused several suitors and walks in her sleep. At Whitby, Mina has met the sceptical old sailor Mr. Swales, and Dr. Seward has been studying his patient Renfield. A storm then drives the Russian schooner Demeter into Whitby harbour with a dead steersman lashed to its wheel. Its log and a bottle message tell of crewmen vanishing one by one and a mate who went mad and jumped overboard, leaving the captain to die at the helm. The cargo is claimed by a local solicitor and a dog is found dead nearby. At the captain's funeral Lucy grows restless, and Mr. Swales is found dead on the churchyard seat. Mina plans to tire Lucy with a long walk. Jonathan's fate and whether the Count has reached England remain unresolved.

A sudden storm breaks over Whitby and a foreign schooner, the Demeter, is driven into the harbour with a dead steersman lashed to its wheel. The ship's log and a message in a bottle reveal that the crew vanished one by one during the voyage and that the mate went mad, believing a tall, pale presence was hidden aboard. The mate jumps overboard, and the captain, left alone, ties himself to the wheel and dies at his post. The Demeter's cargo of earth boxes is claimed by a Whitby solicitor, and the mastiff found dead by the harbour suggests violence. At the captain's funeral Lucy grows restless, and Mr. Swales is found dead on the churchyard seat with a look of terror. Mina notices a dog's terror at the graveside and resolves to tire Lucy with a long walk to stop her sleepwalking.
recaps.title: CHAPTER VII CUTTING FROM “THE DAILYGRAPH,” 8 AUGUST

recaps.text: A young English solicitor, Jonathan Harker, travelled to Transylvania to help Count Dracula buy London property, was held prisoner in the Count's castle, discovered he is a monster, and escaped. In England Mina Murray waits anxiously for word from Jonathan, while her friend Lucy Westenra, who walks in her sleep, is courted by Arthur and others. At Whitby a storm drove the Russian schooner Demeter into the harbour with its dead steersman lashed to the wheel, and old Mr. Swales was later found dead on the churchyard seat. Lucy's mother has been told she may die soon, and Lucy grows weaker. Mina has now learned that Jonathan has been gravely ill in Buda-Pesth and is preparing to go to him. Renfield, in Dr. Seward's asylum, has grown frantic, escaped, and been restrained after claiming his Master is near. The fate of Jonathan and whether Dracula has reached England remain unresolved.

Billington & Son arranges for fifty boxes to be delivered to Carfax, and the carriers confirm the delivery was made as instructed. Lucy's mother privately tells Mina she has a failing heart and little time left, and Mina keeps this from Lucy. Lucy's wedding to Arthur is set to proceed soon because his father has recovered. Lucy grows weaker and her throat wounds fail to heal, and Mina fears for her health. Mina finally receives word of Jonathan, who has been seriously ill, and she prepares to travel to Buda-Pesth to nurse him. Sister Agatha writes that Jonathan's delirium was full of frightening visions and that he must be kept calm. Renfield turns haughty and declares the Master is near, then escapes his room at night. Renfield is caught at the chapel of Carfax, claiming to serve his Master, and is then restrained in a padded room.
recaps.title: CHAPTER VIII MINA MURRAY’S JOURNAL

recaps.text: Jonathan Harker escaped Count Dracula's castle, and in England a monster-linked chain of deaths began at Whitby, including the Demeter's dead steersman and old Mr. Swales. Lucy Westenra has been weakened by a failing health and Dracula's influence, and her mother has been told she has a failing heart. Mina Murray has married Jonathan in Buda-Pesth, where he was gravely ill with brain fever, and she has sealed his secret note-book unread. Lucy, now recovered at Whitby, is engaged to Arthur. Back in London, Dr. Seward finds Lucy physically sound but worsening and calls in Van Helsing, who examines her and says a cause must exist. Renfield, Seward's asylum patient, has escaped repeatedly and is linked to a 'Master' and to the sun and moon. Unresolved: Lucy's cause, Renfield's connection to Dracula, and whether Dracula has reached England.

Mina writes from Buda-Pesth that Jonathan is weak and has lost memory of his recent ordeal, and their marriage takes place there. Jonathan gives Mina his note-book and asks that she keep it sealed, and she wraps it and seals it with her ring. Lucy writes from Whitby that she has recovered her health and is happily engaged to Arthur, with the wedding set for 28 September. Renfield grows calm at moonrise but escapes again and is recaptured at the old chapel, where he calms after watching a bat. Arthur asks Dr. Seward to examine Lucy, whose health is failing, while her mother has been privately told her heart is failing. Seward finds no physical disease in Lucy, suspects a mental cause, and summons Van Helsing, whom he trusts completely. Van Helsing examines Lucy, finds no functional cause, and says he must think before returning if needed. Renfield's violent fits seem linked to times of day, and Seward wonders whether the sun affects him. Seward warns Van Helsing that Renfield has taken a terrible turn and asks him to come at once.
recaps.title: CHAPTER IX

recaps.text: Dracula's voyage to England brought a chain of deaths at Whitby, and Lucy Westenra, who is loved by Arthur Holmwood, has been weakening. Her mother has been told she has a failing heart. Dr. John Seward, who runs an asylum, has called in his old master Van Helsing to examine her, and they found no ordinary cause. Renfield, Seward's patient, is linked to a 'Master' and has escaped repeatedly. Lucy's condition has grown dangerously worse; she was near death, and two blood transfusions have been given, first by Arthur and then by Seward. Van Helsing has found two small punctures on her throat that no one can explain, and he has now placed garlic in her room as protection. Van Helsing is secretive and insists that Arthur must not be told. Unresolved are the cause of Lucy's illness, the meaning of the punctures and garlic, Renfield's connection to Dracula, and whether Dracula has reached England.

Seward meets Van Helsing in London and they agree not to tell Arthur, keeping their knowledge private. Lucy's condition worsens sharply, and Van Helsing decides a blood transfusion must be given at once. Arthur arrives unexpectedly and gives his blood for Lucy's transfusion, which restores some strength to her. Van Helsing and Seward notice two small punctures on Lucy's throat and cannot explain them. Van Helsing leaves for Amsterdam and orders Seward to keep watch, and Lucy sleeps well that night. Lucy is found near death the next morning, and Seward gives his own blood in a second transfusion. Van Helsing swears Seward to silence and then fills Lucy's room with garlic and places a garlic wreath on her neck. Seward is left uneasy by Van Helsing's confidence and his unexplained remedies.
recaps.title: CHAPTER X

recaps.text: Dracula's voyage brought deaths at Whitby, and Lucy Westenra, loved by Arthur Holmwood, has been weakening under an unexplained illness. Dr. John Seward, who runs an asylum, called in his old master Van Helsing, who found two punctures on Lucy's throat and set garlic and flowers about her room as protection. Two blood transfusions, from Arthur and then Seward, have given her temporary strength, and Van Helsing has kept the truth from Arthur. Renfield, Seward's patient, is linked to a 'Master' and attacked Seward with a knife, cutting his wrist. Lucy's mother unknowingly removed the protective flowers and later died of fright when a wolf broke through the window, while the maids were drugged. Lucy, alone and believing she is dying, has written a memorandum. Unresolved are the cause of Lucy's illness, the meaning of the punctures, Renfield's connection to Dracula, and whether Dracula has reached England.

Lucy's mother unknowingly removes the protective flowers from Lucy's room, which Van Helsing learns about with despair. Van Helsing and Seward perform another transfusion on Lucy, and Van Helsing takes charge of her night watch. Lucy recovers and reports peaceful days, while Van Helsing travels briefly to Amsterdam. Separately, the escaped wolf Bersicker is discussed by the zoo keeper, then returns to his cage on his own. Renfield attacks Seward with a knife and cuts his wrist, leaving Seward weakened and worried. Van Helsing's urgent telegram arrives too late, and Seward fears that a night has been lost. That night Lucy's mother dies of fright when a wolf breaks through the window, and the maids are drugged. Lucy, alone with her mother's body, writes a memorandum believing she is dying and bids farewell to Arthur.
recaps.title: CHAPTER XI

recaps.text: Dracula's voyage brought deaths at Whitby, and Lucy Westenra, loved by Arthur Holmwood, has been weakening under an unexplained illness. Van Helsing, called in by Dr. Seward, found punctures on Lucy's throat and guarded her with garlic and flowers. Two transfusions, from Arthur and then Seward, gave her temporary strength. Renfield, Seward's patient, is linked to a 'Master' and attacked Seward, cutting his wrist. Lucy's mother unknowingly removed the protective flowers and died of fright after a wolf broke through the window, while the maids were drugged. Seward and Van Helsing forced their way into the house and revived Lucy with brandy and warmth. Quincey Morris arrived and gave his blood for a third transfusion. Lucy then died after a strange, predatory change, and Van Helsing warned that her death is only the beginning. Unresolved are the cause of Lucy's illness, the meaning of the punctures, Renfield's connection to Dracula, and whether Dracula has reached England.

Seward finds Lucy's house silent and enters with Van Helsing through a kitchen window, discovering the maids drugged and Lucy's mother dead. Van Helsing revives Lucy with brandy and warmth, and the maids prepare a bath to restore her. Quincey Morris arrives in answer to Arthur's telegram and gives his blood in another transfusion, which steadies Lucy. Van Helsing shows Seward a paper from Lucy's breast, and Seward is baffled, but Van Helsing asks him to set it aside. Seward plans to certify Mrs. Westenra's death as heart disease to avoid an inquest and arranges her undertaker. Quincey questions Seward about Lucy's illness and learns that Arthur and others have given blood, deepening his fear. Arthur arrives at Hillingham, and Lucy briefly rallies to speak with him before her strength fades again. At dawn Van Helsing finds Lucy's throat wounds gone and declares her dying, and her behaviour grows strange and predatory. Van Helsing stops Arthur from kissing Lucy, and she asks him to guard Arthur before she dies. Lucy dies, and Van Helsing warns Seward that her death is not the end but only the beginning.
recaps.title: CHAPTER XII DR. SEWARD’S DIARY

recaps.text: Dracula's voyage brought deaths at Whitby, and Lucy Westenra, loved by Arthur Holmwood, weakened under an unexplained illness with two punctures on her throat. Van Helsing guarded her with garlic and flowers and arranged transfusions from Arthur, Seward and Quincey Morris. Mrs. Westenra died after the protective flowers were removed, and Lucy died after a predatory change, with Van Helsing warning that her death was only the beginning. Lucy is now buried in the family tomb and Arthur inherits her mother's estate. Van Helsing holds Lucy's papers and has persuaded Arthur to trust him, and he and Seward have called off a plan to open the coffin. In London, Jonathan has glimpsed a dark stranger he believes is the Count, which has left him shaken. Newspapers report children on Hampstead Heath lured away by a 'bloofer lady' with throat wounds. Unresolved are the cause of Lucy's illness, the meaning of the punctures, Renfield's connection to Dracula, and whether Dracula is in England.

Van Helsing reveals that the crucifix on Lucy's mouth was stolen and recovered, so the grim operation is called off. Mrs. Westenra's solicitor reveals that her entire estate has passed to Arthur, which the family's lawyers had tried to prevent. Arthur grieves at Lucy's bedside, kissing her hand and forehead before leaving her in the coffin. Van Helsing asks Arthur for trust and for permission to keep Lucy's papers, and Arthur agrees. In London, Mina and Jonathan attend Mr. Hawkins's funeral, and Jonathan sees the dark stranger in Piccadilly and is terrified it is the man himself. Mina receives a telegram announcing that Mrs. Westenra and Lucy are dead and buried. Van Helsing confesses to Seward that his grief shows as laughter and that he knows a reason for his sorrow he cannot share.
recaps.title: CHAPTER XIII DR. SEWARD’S DIARY—continued.

recaps.text: Dracula's voyage brought deaths at Whitby, and Lucy Westenra, loved by Arthur Holmwood, weakened under an unexplained illness with two punctures on her throat. Van Helsing guarded her with garlic and flowers and arranged transfusions from Arthur, Seward and Quincey Morris. Mrs. Westenra died after the protective flowers were removed, and Lucy died after a predatory change, with Van Helsing warning her death was only the beginning. Lucy is buried and Arthur inherits the estate. In London, Jonathan glimpsed a dark stranger he believes is the Count and was shaken. Mina, now married to Jonathan, met Van Helsing in Exeter, gave him her diary copies, and he reassured Jonathan that his journal is true. Van Helsing returned to London alarmed by newspaper reports of children with throat wounds, and told Seward that Lucy made those punctures. Unresolved: how Lucy came to this state, Renfield's link to Dracula, whether Dracula is in England, and what Van Helsing will do next.

Van Helsing visits Mina in Exeter at her invitation, and she shows him her shorthand diary, then a typewritten copy. Van Helsing reads Lucy's diary account of her sleepwalking and the rescue, and praises Mina warmly. Mina pleads with Van Helsing to restore Jonathan, and he comforts her and promises to help. Van Helsing reads Jonathan's journal and assures Mina it is true and that Jonathan is sound in mind and heart. Jonathan meets Van Helsing in Exeter, is reassured by his letter, and agrees to help him learn what happened in Transylvania. Van Helsing sees a newspaper report in the Westminster Gazette and leaves for London looking shaken. Seward learns from Van Helsing that the children's throat wounds resemble Lucy's, and Van Helsing hints at a worse cause than an ordinary animal. Van Helsing says the wounds on the children were made by Lucy, leaving Seward appalled.
recaps.title: CHAPTER XIV MINA HARKER’S JOURNAL

recaps.text: Van Helsing tells Seward that Lucy is Un-Dead and asks him to prove it at the churchyard. At the hospital, Dr. Vincent shows the child's punctures, which match Lucy's, and Van Helsing gives them no explanation. At night, the two men open the Westenra tomb and find Lucy's coffin empty. In the churchyard they rescue a sleeping child from a white figure and leave the child for a policeman. The next day they reopen the tomb and find Lucy's body fresh, with sharpened teeth, which convinces Seward. Van Helsing explains that Lucy's Un-Dead state differs from others and that he must stake her in her sleep, and Seward half accepts this. Van Helsing delays the staking, writes a note in case he dies, and plans a vigil and a gathering of the men. Arthur and Quincey agree to Van Helsing's request in confidence, but Arthur balks at mutilating Lucy's body. Van Helsing explains that Lucy may be Un-Dead and asks Arthur to witness the tomb, and Arthur agrees to go with him to wait.
recaps.title: CHAPTER XV DR. SEWARD’S DIARY—continued.

recaps.text: Dracula's voyage brought deaths at Whitby, and Lucy Westenra, loved by Arthur Holmwood, weakened under an unexplained illness with two punctures on her throat. Van Helsing guarded her with garlic and flowers and arranged transfusions from Arthur, Seward and Quincey Morris. Mrs. Westenra died, and Lucy died after a predatory change, with Van Helsing warning that her death was only the beginning. Jonathan glimpsed a dark stranger he believes is the Count, and Van Helsing reassured him that Mina's record is true. Van Helsing confirmed that Lucy is Un-Dead, and the men opened her tomb to find it empty. They rescued a child from a white figure, and the next day Lucy's body was found fresh with sharpened teeth. The night after, Arthur drove a stake through Lucy's heart in her tomb while Van Helsing read the prayers, and her body was then beheaded and resealed. Van Helsing has asked Seward, Arthur and Quincey to help him find the author of their sorrow, and each has promised to see it through. Van Helsing has left for Amsterdam and will return to plan the next steps, and the question of Dracula's presence in England remains unresolved.

The men find Lucy's coffin empty, and Van Helsing explains that the Un-Dead can move at sundown. In the churchyard Lucy appears with a child, and she tries to lure Arthur to her before Van Helsing drives her back with his crucifix. Van Helsing seals the tomb with consecrated wafers, and Lucy's body re-enters through a gap too small for a knife. The next night the men return and Van Helsing explains that Lucy must be staked to free her soul. Arthur volunteers to drive the stake into Lucy's heart, and the body writhes before lying still. Lucy's face appears peaceful and as it was in life, and Arthur kisses her before she is beheaded and sealed in her coffin. Van Helsing asks the men to help him find the author of their sorrow, and each promises to see the quest through. Van Helsing arranges to dine with Seward and Arthur in two nights and leaves for Amsterdam to prepare.
recaps.title: CHAPTER XVI DR. SEWARD’S DIARY—continued

recaps.text: Mina arrives in London and meets Seward, who is reluctant to let her hear his phonograph diary of Lucy's death. Mina persuades Seward to let her type the cylinders, and she and Jonathan order all the evidence chronologically. Seward notes Renfield's unusual calm and suspects it is linked to the Count's presence. Jonathan travels to Whitby and London and confirms that fifty boxes of earth were delivered to Carfax. Lord Godalming and Quincey Morris arrive early, and Mina tells them she has read and typed all the papers. Lord Godalming breaks down in grief, and Mina comforts him as a sister would, earning his lasting gratitude. Quincey Morris is moved by Mina's kindness and kisses her hand, so the group is now united around the shared record.
recaps.title: CHAPTER XVII DR. SEWARD’S DIARY—continued

recaps.text: Dracula's voyage brought deaths at Whitby, and Lucy Westenra died after a predatory change. Van Helsing confirmed Lucy was Un-Dead and had her staked and beheaded, then asked Seward, Arthur and Quincey to join him against the vampire. Mina and Jonathan have arranged the evidence, and the men have pledged themselves to the campaign. The council traced the fifty boxes of earth to the house next to Seward's, and the men went to search it while keeping Mina out of danger. Renfield, the asylum patient, unexpectedly pleaded for release before collapsing when refused. Where things stand: the men are searching the house at Carfax, Mina waits behind, and the vampire's whereabouts and the fate of the remaining boxes are unresolved.

Mina visits Renfield, who unexpectedly speaks with great courtesy and philosophical clarity before blessing her as she leaves. Van Helsing arrives and learns that Dracula bought the house next to Seward's, which he regrets not having known earlier. The council convenes, and each man pledges to join the campaign against the vampire, with Mina acting as secretary. Van Helsing explains the vampire's history, powers and limits, and how he may be found and destroyed. A shot is fired outside the window and a bat is shot at, Morris explaining that he has been hunting such creatures. The men resolve to trace the fifty boxes of earth and to keep Mina out of the danger ahead. Renfield summons Seward urgently and, in an unusually rational manner, begs to be released for reasons he says he cannot fully explain. Seward refuses, and Renfield's pleas grow frantic until he collapses, calmed by the doctor's firm command.
recaps.title: CHAPTER XVIII DR. SEWARD’S DIARY

recaps.text: Dracula's voyage brought deaths at Whitby, and Lucy Westenra died after a predatory change, was staked and beheaded by Van Helsing. Van Helsing, Seward, Arthur, Quincey and Mina formed a council against the vampire, and the men pledged to hunt him. Mina has been kept out of the danger. The council traced fifty boxes of earth to the Carfax house beside Seward's asylum. The men searched the house and chapel, finding twenty-nine boxes still present and driving off rats with the terriers. Renfield, the asylum patient, has refused to speak to Van Helsing. Mina weeps over Lucy's death and has had a frightening dream. The vampire's whereabouts and the fate of the remaining boxes are unresolved, and the men continue their work without Mina.

The men search the Carfax house and its chapel, finding twenty-nine of the fifty earth-boxes still present. Rats swarm the chapel until Lord Godalming releases the terriers, which drive them off. The search of the rest of the house finds only dust and untouched rooms. Van Helsing concludes that twenty-one boxes are known to be removed and that the Count is likely elsewhere. Van Helsing visits Renfield, who insults him and refuses to speak, ending the chance of learning from him. Mina weeps over Lucy's death and resolves to hide her distress from Jonathan. Mina has a frightening dream of a mist entering the room, and she takes a sleeping draught from Seward. The men continue tracing the boxes, while Mina remains excluded from the campaign.
recaps.title: CHAPTER XIX JONATHAN HARKER’S JOURNAL

recaps.text: Bloxam describes an old, unnaturally strong helper who lifted the boxes, pointing to the Count handling the earth himself. Harker finds the Piccadilly house empty and decides to keep his findings from Mina for her safety. Mitchell, Sons & Candy reveal that a Count de Ville bought the house for cash. Renfield speaks with cunning about life and souls and claims he will never lack the means of life. Renfield is found bloodied after a wild yell, leaving the men uncertain what happened.
recaps.title: CHAPTER XX JONATHAN HARKER’S JOURNAL

recaps.text: Renfield lies gravely injured and Van Helsing decides to trephine his skull while the attendant is sent away. Renfield wakes briefly and confesses that the Count came to his window and was let in, and that he himself resisted and was flung down. The company rushes to the Harkers' room and finds the Count feeding on Mina while Jonathan lies in a drugged stupor. Van Helsing raises the Sacred Wafer and the Count flees, leaving Mina shamed and Jonathan horrified. Mina recounts how the Count drank from her, forced her to drink his blood, and bound her to his call. Arthur reports that the Count burned the manuscript and the phonograph cylinders, and that Renfield has died. Morris saw a bat fly west from Renfield's window, so the Count has likely gone to another lair. The group agrees to act quickly, and one of them will stay with the Harkers until they can plan.
recaps.title: CHAPTER XXI DR. SEWARD’S DIARY

recaps.text: Renfield is found dead with his neck broken, and Seward decides to certify the death as a fall from bed to avoid the truth coming out. Mina insists on being told everything and resolves to face her fate, and Van Helsing forbids her to die until the Count is destroyed. Van Helsing reasons that the Count can only be found in the daylight hours and proposes entering the Piccadilly house with a locksmith. Mina insists that the men go to Piccadilly, and the group prepares to split into two parties. As Van Helsing places the Sacred Wafer on Mina's forehead, it burns her flesh and leaves a scar she believes marks her as unclean. The men pledge to protect Mina, and the group swears to be true to each other and prays for guidance. At Carfax the group sterilises the earth boxes there by placing Sacred Wafers in them, hoping to deny the Count his lairs. At Piccadilly a locksmith opens the door, and the group finds eight earth boxes and the Count's papers, though one box is still unaccounted for. Godalming and Morris take the keys and leave to destroy the boxes in the East and South, while the rest wait for their return.
recaps.title: CHAPTER XXII JONATHAN HARKER’S JOURNAL

recaps.text: The men wait for Godalming and Morris, and Harker sinks deeper into despair. A telegram from Mina warns that the Count has left Carfax and may come to them. Godalming and Morris return, having destroyed the boxes they searched for. The Count bursts in, Harker attacks him, and the Count escapes through the window. The Count vows revenge over centuries and flees into the stable, leaving the men without him. The men burn the remaining papers and return to Mina, with one earth-box still unaccounted for. Mina urges pity for the Count and Harker vows to destroy him, showing their divided feelings. Mina asks to be hypnotised, and under the trance she describes being aboard a ship. Van Helsing concludes the Count plans to escape London by sea and resolves to follow him. Van Helsing warns Mina that the Count's mark makes her time dangerous, and she faints.
recaps.title: CHAPTER XXIII DR. SEWARD’S DIARY

recaps.text: Dracula's voyage brought deaths at Whitby, and Lucy Westenra died after a predatory change; Van Helsing staked and beheaded her. Van Helsing, Seward, Arthur, Quincey and Mina formed a council and the men pledged to hunt the vampire. The council traced fifty earth-boxes to Carfax, where twenty-nine remained, and the Count escaped Harker's attack in London and fled. Mina has been kept out of the danger but is marked on her forehead and fears the Count's hold on her. Van Helsing has traced the Count to the Czarina Catherine, bound for Varna, and the company plans to follow overland, arriving before the ship. Mina has insisted on joining the journey and made Harker promise not to reveal the plans. The party will leave for Varna by the 17th, armed, to board the ship and destroy the box.

Van Helsing reports to Harker by phonograph that the Count has fled to Transylvania and that the company will follow him. Van Helsing's party traces the Count to the Czarina Catherine, a ship bound for Varna, and learns from its crew that a tall pale man shipped a great box aboard her. Mina insists on joining the journey, fearing the Count could compel her to reveal the plans, and Van Helsing agrees to take her. The company resolves to leave for Varna by the 17th, arm themselves with Winchesters, and destroy the box on board. Harker is troubled that his wife will not take part in discussing the plans and makes a promise not to tell her what is planned. Morris vows to destroy the box at once whatever the risk, and Harker settles his affairs, naming Mina his sole heir.
recaps.title: CHAPTER XXIV DR. SEWARD’S PHONOGRAPH DIARY, SPOKEN BY VAN HELSING

recaps.text: Dracula's voyage brought deaths at Whitby, and Lucy Westenra died after a predatory change; Van Helsing staked and beheaded her. A council of Van Helsing, Seward, Arthur, Quincey and Mina formed, and the men pledged to hunt the vampire. The council traced fifty earth-boxes to Carfax, and the Count fled London. Mina has been marked by the Sacred Wafer and fears the Count's hold on her, and the company has pledged to kill her if she becomes a vampire. The company tracked the Count to the Czarina Catherine bound for Varna, and waited there for the ship. It arrived but then continued on to Galatz, and the company is preparing to follow by train at dawn. Van Helsing suspects the Count used Mina's mind, while Mina feels her soul freer than before. The company now plans to pursue the Count to Galatz.

Van Helsing recounts the company's preparations in Varna, where they wait for the ship while Mina's trance reports keep describing waves and wind. On learning that the Czarina Catherine has entered Galatz, the company is shocked and reorganises for a train journey at dawn. Mina reveals her knowledge of the train times, and Van Helsing hopes her new clarity will help them track the Count. Van Helsing confides to Seward that the Count may have used Mina's mind during her trance, and he believes the Count's selfishness will be his undoing. Mina realises the Count has isolated himself from her, and she feels freer than since the night he marked her. Van Helsing asks Seward to record everything so the men can read it upon their return, and Mina types the notes.
recaps.title: CHAPTER XXV DR. SEWARD’S DIARY

recaps.text: Dracula's voyage brought deaths at Whitby, and Lucy Westenra died after a predatory change; Van Helsing staked and beheaded her. A council of Van Helsing, Seward, Arthur, Quincey and Mina formed, and the men pledged to hunt the vampire. The council traced fifty earth-boxes to Carfax, and the Count fled London. Mina has been marked by the Sacred Wafer and fears the Count's hold on her. The company tracked the Czarina Catherine to Galatz, where Immanuel Hildesheim received the Count's box and passed it to Petrof Skinsky, who was later found murdered. Mina deduced the box is moving by river toward the Count's castle, and the company split: Godalming and Harker pursue by launch, Seward and Morris ride the bank, and Van Helsing and Mina drive toward the Borgo Pass. Things stand with the launch delayed at the rapids and the carriage party about seventy miles from the pass, with the box still unrecovered and somewhere on the water ahead of the men.

The company learns from the Czarina Catherine's skipper that the box was taken off the ship before dawn by Immanuel Hildesheim under the name of Count Dracula. Hildesheim passed the box to Petrof Skinsky, a Slovak trader, and the company loses track of it when Skinsky disappears. Skinsky's body is found in a churchyard with its throat torn open, leaving the party without a lead and forced to reconsider their plan. Mina works out from the trance reports and the map that the box is likely travelling by boat up the Sereth and the Bistritza toward the Count's castle. Van Helsing chooses to lead Mina overland to the Borgo Pass while the men pursue the box by steam launch and on horseback along the river. Godalming and Harker race upstream in the launch, but they find no sign of the box and pass many small boats without success. At Fundu they hear that a fast boat with a double crew passed in the night, confirming the box is ahead of them. The launch is held up by an accident on the rapids, delaying the pursuit, while Mina and Van Helsing buy a carriage at Veresti for the drive to the pass.
recaps.title: CHAPTER XXVI DR. SEWARD’S DIARY

recaps.text: Dracula's voyage brought deaths at Whitby, and Lucy Westenra died after a predatory change, was staked and beheaded by Van Helsing. A council formed against the Count, who fled London, and his earth-boxes were traced by ship and river. The company split, with Godalming and Harker pursuing the box by launch and Seward and Morris riding the bank, while Van Helsing led Mina overland to the Borgo Pass. Mina directed the route, and the Count's vampire women tried to draw her in, but she remained within the Holy circle. Van Helsing destroyed the three women and banished Dracula from his tomb. Mina and Van Helsing then headed east on foot as Jonathan and his companions intercepted the gypsy cart. At sunset Jonathan and Morris killed the Count in the box, and Morris died of his wound. The Count is dead, Morris is dead, and Mina's forehead is now marked by the Sacred Wafer's scar, which Morris declares a sign the curse has lifted.

Van Helsing and Mina drive through the mountains toward the Borgo Pass, with Mina directing the route from Jonathan's diary and hypnotised each sunset. Caught in a snowstorm at night, Mina stays within the Holy circle as the three vampire women try to draw her to them. Van Helsing climbs to the castle, destroys the three women by staking and beheading them, and banishes Dracula from his tomb with the Sacred Wafer. Mina and Van Helsing set out on foot toward the east, where they expect Jonathan to be, and find shelter among rocks. From their vantage they see the gypsy cart carrying the box and watch the men converge on it from all sides. Jonathan and Morris break open the box at sunset, and the Count dies when Jonathan cuts his throat and Morris pierces his heart. The gypsies flee, and the wolves follow them away from the company. Morris, dying of a wound in his side, declares the curse has passed as the sun sets on Mina's forehead, then dies.
recaps.title: CHAPTER XXVII MINA HARKER’S JOURNAL

recaps.text: Dracula's voyage brought deaths at Whitby, and Lucy Westenra died after a predatory change and was staked and beheaded by Van Helsing. A council formed against the Count, who fled London, and the companions pursued his earth-boxes by river and road. At the Borgo Pass, Van Helsing held Mina within the Holy circle while the Count's vampire women tried to draw her away, and Van Helsing destroyed them and banished Dracula from his tomb. At sunset Jonathan Harker and Quincey Morris killed the Count in his box, and Morris died of his wound. Mina bears the Sacred Wafer's scar on her forehead, which Morris called a sign the curse has lifted. Years later the survivors, now settled and married, revisit Transylvania and collect their papers, and they admit that the record would never convince an outsider. The story now rests on their memories and on the boy named after Quincey.
The companions gather the papers from their safe and realise there is almost no authentic document among them, only typed records and private note-books.
recaps.title: NOTE
